title: Valuative base change lifting the generic points of two closure fibres
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $y\in X$, $t=f(y)$, and let $Y=\overline{\{y\}}\subseteq X$ with its reduced integral closed-subscheme structure [def-pc-integral-scheme]. For $s\in S$ let $x$ be the generic point [def-sc-generic-point] of an irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of the fibre $Y_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. There exist a valuation ring $A$ (an integral domain such that for each nonzero element $a$ of its fraction field either $a\in A$ or $a^{-1}\in A$), a morphism $g:S'=\operatorname{Spec}A\to S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and, in the base-change square $X'=X\times_SS'$ with projections $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S'$ [def-pc-base-change], points $y',x'\in X'$ with the following properties. Writing $t'$ and $s'$ for the generic and closed points of $S'$, one has $g(t')=t$, $g(s')=s$; $y'\in X'_{t'}$ is generic in an irreducible component of $Y_t\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t')$ and $g'(y')=y$; and, if $Y'=\overline{\{y'\}}\subseteq X'$ has its reduced integral closed-subscheme structure, then $x'\in Y'_{s'}$ is generic in an irreducible component of $Y'_{s'}$ and $g'(x')=x$. Residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field].

proof.text: Because $x$ lies in the fibre of the reduced closure $Y=\overline{\{y\}}$, the point $y$ specializes to $x$. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-ring-specialization-lift] to obtain a valuation ring $A$, its spectrum $S' =\operatorname{Spec}A$, and a morphism $h:S'\to X$ whose generic point maps to $y$ and whose closed point maps to $x$. Define $g=f\circ h$. Then $g(t')=t$ and $g(s')=s$, where $t'$ and $s'$ are the generic and closed points of $S'.$

source.place: Tag 0GSH, proof first paragraph: choose a valuation ring and a morphism from its spectrum realizing the specialization (Schemes, Lemma 01J8, schemes-lemma-points-specialize); set g=f∘h.

proof.text: Form the Cartesian square $X'=X\times_SS'$ with projections $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S'.$ The map $h$ gives a section $\sigma:S'\to X'$ of $f'$ by the universal property of the fibre product, and since $h$ factors through $Y$, the section factors through $S'\times_SY$.

source.place: Tag 0GSH, proof first paragraph: consider the base change and obtain a section; the section factors through the base change of Y.

proof.text: Choose an irreducible component of the fibre $(S'\times_SY)_{t'}=Y_t\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t')$ containing $\sigma(t')$, and let $y'$ be its generic point. Since $g'(y')$ lies in $Y_t$ and specializes to $g'(\sigma(t'))=y$, while $y$ is the generic point of the irreducible fibre $Y_t$ (every point of $Y_t$ is a specialization of the generic point $y$), one has $g'(y')=y$. Thus $y'$ is generic in an irreducible component of the indicated generic fibre and maps to $y$.

source.place: Tag 0GSH, proof second paragraph: choose y′ over the component containing σ(t′), then use genericity of y to conclude g′(y′)=y.

proof.text: Let $Y'\subseteq X'$ be the reduced closure of $\{y'\}$. The section $\sigma$ factors through $Y'$ because $\sigma(t')$ lies in the closure of $\{y'\}$. Choose an irreducible component of $Y'_{s'}$ containing $\sigma(s')$ and let $x'$ be its generic point. Then $x'$ specializes to $\sigma(s')$, so $g'(x')$ specializes to $g'(\sigma(s'))=x$. Since $g'(Y')\subseteq Y$ and $x$ is the generic point of an irreducible component of $Y_s$, this forces $g'(x')=x$. This gives the required special-fibre component lift and completes all clauses.

source.place: Tag 0GSH, proof third paragraph: form Y′, choose x′ over the component containing σ(s′), and conclude g′(x′)=x by genericity.

lean.statement: theorem exists_valuative_fibre_component_lift {X S Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (y : X) (i : Y ⟶ X) [IsIntegral Y] [IsClosedImmersion i] (hY : Set.range i = closure ({y} : Set X)) (s : S) (x : (i ≫ f).fiber s) (C : Set ((i ≫ f).fiber s)) (hC : C ∈ irreducibleComponents ((i ≫ f).fiber s)) (hx : IsGenericPoint x C) : ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : IsDomain A) (_ : ValuationRing A) (g : Spec (CommRingCat.of A) ⟶ S) (t' s' : Spec (CommRingCat.of A)), IsGenericPoint t' Set.univ ∧ IsClosed ({s'} : Set (Spec (CommRingCat.of A))) ∧ g t' = f y ∧ g s' = s ∧ ∃ (z : (pullback.snd (i ≫ f) g).fiber t') (D : Set ((pullback.snd (i ≫ f) g).fiber t')), D ∈ irreducibleComponents ((pullback.snd (i ≫ f) g).fiber t') ∧ IsGenericPoint z D ∧ ∃ y' : (pullback f g : Scheme.{u}), (pullback.snd f g) y' = t' ∧ (pullback.fst f g) y' = y ∧ (pullback.map (i ≫ f) g f g i (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _) (Category.comp_id _) ((Category.comp_id g).trans (Category.id_comp g).symm)) ((pullback.snd (i ≫ f) g).fiberι t' z) = y' ∧ ∃ (Y' : Scheme.{u}) (_ : IsIntegral Y') (i' : Y' ⟶ pullback f g) (_ : IsClosedImmersion i'), Set.range i' = closure ({y'} : Set (pullback f g : Scheme.{u})) ∧ ∃ (x' : (i' ≫ pullback.snd f g).fiber s') (E : Set ((i' ≫ pullback.snd f g).fiber s')), E ∈ irreducibleComponents ((i' ≫ pullback.snd f g).fiber s') ∧ IsGenericPoint x' E ∧ (pullback.fst f g) (i' ((i' ≫ pullback.snd f g).fiberι s' x')) = i ((i ≫ f).fiberι s x)
lean.note: The reduced integral closures are presented by integral closed immersions with image equal to the singleton closure. This uniquely specifies the reduced induced closed-subscheme structure up to its unique ambient isomorphism. All component points are points of actual scheme-theoretic fibres; the canonical pullback.map identifies the generic-fibre point with the ambient lifted point.
